theme: Academic replication packages using Airbnb data: Zervas Proserpio Byers (hotel impact), Barron Kung Proserpio (housing), Farronato Fradkin, Horn Merante, Garcia-Lopez Barcelona, Koster Los Angeles, Edelman discrimination, Fradkin reviews

candidates.name: tomslee/airbnb-data-collection
candidates.what_it_holds: Python/PostgreSQL scraper for Airbnb listing pages (surveys). No data committed in the repo itself, but the author's linked data page (tomslee.net/airbnb-data-collection-get-the-data) hosts zip files of CSV 'surveys' for dozens of cities collected periodically from Oct 2013 through late 2017 -- this is the dataset that predates Inside Airbnb and was used as an input/comparator in several early sharing-economy academic papers (pre-2018 Airbnb listing snapshots). MIT license. Last active ~2019 (maintainer states no longer maintained; issues since 2019 unresolved).
candidates.why_useful: Fills gap #1 (historical/archived Airbnb dumps older than what Inside Airbnb's CDN retains) -- covers 2013-2017, years for which we have no Inside Airbnb coverage at all. Also relevant to gap #2 (historical listing/price snapshots) as a point-in-time series of city-level surveys, several years earlier than our current panel start (Dec 2022).
candidates.geography: Dozens of cities globally (city list on tomslee.net)
candidates.license: MIT (code); data hosted externally, licence for the zips not stated
candidates.size_hint: Multiple city zip files of CSV surveys, several years each; exact size not confirmed (external host, not verified live)

candidates.name: montera34/airbnb.barcelona
candidates.what_it_holds: Repo from a 2018 participatory data workshop on Airbnb/touristification in Barcelona. Contains Inside-Airbnb-sourced snapshots under data/original/airbnb/ at multiple dated pulls between 150430 (30 Apr 2015) and 190308 (8 Mar 2019), each with listings_summary_barcelona_insideairbnb.csv and reviews_summary_barcelona_insideairbnb.csv (large listings.csv.gz not stored in repo), plus geographic boundary shapefiles and Barcelona demographic/housing (population, dwelling) tables for overlay analysis.
candidates.why_useful: Barcelona Inside Airbnb history back to April 2015 -- earlier than our current 13-city panel (Dec 2022 onward) and directly relevant to the Garcia-Lopez et al. Barcelona housing-impact replication literature named in this theme; also usable to sanity-check current Barcelona ADR/listing trends against a much longer base period.
candidates.license: Not explicit in README (montera34 projects are typically open-data oriented; verify before use)
candidates.size_hint: Multiple dated snapshot folders of listings/reviews summary CSVs plus shapefiles
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Partial overlap with our Barcelona Inside Airbnb coverage, but several years older

candidates.name: UPGo-McGill/strr
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (from David Wachsmuth's UPGo Lab at McGill, the group behind the Airbnb-and-the-rent-gap / gentrification literature adjacent to this theme) providing functions to clean/compress/expand raw AirDNA property and daily files, detect multi-listing commercial operators (strr_multi), frequently-rented entire-home listings (strr_FREH), 'ghost hostel' clusters of private rooms in one building (strr_ghost), classify listings as real housing units (strr_housing), and estimate true listing locations from fuzzy map pins (strr_raffle). No large datasets committed; this is a processing/analysis toolkit meant to be pointed at AirDNA or Inside-Airbnb-shaped inputs. Actively developed (400+ commits).
candidates.why_useful: Directly implements the STR housing/commercial-operator/ghost-hostel detection methodology used across the Wachsmuth/Barron-Kung-Proserpio-adjacent housing literature named in this theme; could be run over our own Inside Airbnb 13-city or 120-market panels to derive commercial-host-share and ghost-listing metrics as supply-quality proxies, relevant to gap #2 (occupancy/pricing realism) and general supply-side signal construction.
candidates.geography: Method is geography-agnostic (built on Canadian STR work, generalizable)
candidates.license: Not stated in fetched content (check repo LICENSE file before use)
candidates.size_hint: R package source, no bundled data
candidates.last_activity: Active (UPGo Lab ongoing research org, multiple 2023-2024 report repos)

candidates.what_it_holds: Active academic urban-research GitHub org (McGill School of Urban Planning, David Wachsmuth) with a cluster of yearly report repos analyzing STR and rental-housing markets in Canada, including a Quebec CITQ (STR registration) report repo (citq-rapport-2024), BC and Ontario STR/rental reports, CMHC (Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp) rent panels, and a Montreal landlord-data scraper (mtl_landlords, Python). Individual repos' committed CSVs were not confirmed live (fetch only returned repo listing, not file trees), so treat as a method/organization to mine further rather than a confirmed dataset.
candidates.why_useful: If the CITQ and CMHC repos do commit data, this would be a genuine Canadian STR-registration and rent-panel dataset relevant to gap #12 (STR ordinance/registration trackers -- Quebec CITQ named explicitly there) and gap #7/#13 (Canada StatCan-adjacent, housing/rent panels). Flagging as a cluster worth a deeper look by whichever agent owns the regulatory-tracker or Canada-volume gap.
candidates.size_hint: Unconfirmed -- needs a follow-up file-tree check

candidates.name: Replication data for Edelman, Luca & Svirsky (2016) — Racial Discrimination in the Sharing Economy
candidates.what_it_holds: Official openICPSR replication deposit for the Edelman/Luca/Svirsky field-experiment paper on racial discrimination in Airbnb host acceptance rates (named explicitly in this theme). Not on GitHub itself (no GitHub mirror found in this pass) -- hosted at openicpsr.org project 113691.
candidates.why_useful: Direct primary replication package for one of the eight named papers in this theme; useful as a reference dataset on discrimination/acceptance-rate dynamics even though it predates current forecasting relevance, and as a template for what a proper replication package looks like if the team wants to request similar deposits for the other seven papers.

notes: None of the eight named papers (Zervas/Proserpio/Byers, Barron/Kung/Proserpio, Farronato/Fradkin, Horn/Merante, Garcia-Lopez Barcelona, Koster LA, Edelman discrimination, Fradkin reviews) has a GitHub-hosted replication package -- these are all marketing/economics journal papers whose data-sharing norms (when followed at all) route through openICPSR, journal supplements, or 'available on request' rather than GitHub. Only Edelman/Luca/Svirsky had a locatable formal replication deposit (openICPSR, not GitHub). The productive angle in this theme turned out to be adjacent active research-group GitHub orgs that build on / extend this literature: davide Proserpio's own github.io page (dadepro.github.io) lists papers but no code/data links at all. Tom Slee's pre-Inside-Airbnb scraper/archive (2013-2017) is the best 'older than what we hold' historical find. Barcelona workshop repo (montera34) gives a genuine multi-year-older Barcelona panel. UPGo-McGill (Wachsmuth lab, adjacent gentrification/rent-gap literature, not exactly this theme's named authors but the same intellectual lineage) is the most active current STR-academic GitHub presence and merits a deeper file-tree check by whoever owns the STR-regulation or Canada-volume gaps -- I could not confirm from WebFetch summaries alone whether citq-rapport-2024/cmhc-rent-2023/bc-report-2024 actually commit raw CSVs or just analysis code; this needs `list_files`-style follow-up, which this web-only modality pass could not do reliably (WebFetch summarizes rather than lists a repo's file tree). WebSearch quota for the session was exhausted after 17 queries here, cutting the pass short of the 8-15 target's upper end for verification depth; a couple more targeted searches (Alsudais 'Incorrect Data in Inside Airbnb' paper's own repo, and a direct check of whether Zervas/Byers ever posted a JMR web-appendix with a Texas hotel STR data extract) were queued but not completed.
gap_targets_summary_for_orchestrator: Best candidates against numbered gaps: #1 historical archives (tomslee, montera34/airbnb.barcelona), #12 regulation/registration (UPGo-McGill citq-rapport-2024 pending file-tree confirmation), #2/#9 supply-quality methodology (UPGo-McGill/strr package).
